decisions.reason: The source changes Mint Successful modal messaging, not FAQ content; shared reward terminology does not require an FAQ state change.
The source conditions success-modal copy on referral usage but does not change ticket issuance, weighting, expiration, or reset mechanics.
The source concerns post-mint modal messaging and does not change landing-page hero content or layout.
The modal text describes the already-established random ticket and commission allocation for no-referral mints without changing its trigger, recipient, components, or cardinality.
The source changes an on-site Mint Successful modal and does not address email delivery, confirmation contents, or reward notifications.
Mention of a $5 commission and prize ticket is descriptive modal copy and does not alter primary-mint revenue allocation.
The source specifically changes Mint Successful modal messaging and does not instruct any change to About-page content.
The source does not change how tickets or commissions are recorded in dashboards, leaderboards, NFT attributes, or aggregate accounting.
The reference to an NFT holder receiving a random reward does not change NFT resale or ownership-state transfer semantics.
The source distinguishes modal messages for code-used and no-code mints but does not change which referral codes are eligible or valid.
The source does not address fiat wallet provisioning, dashboard access, purchase confirmation, or reward cashout guidance.
Requiring different success messaging when a referral code is used does not change the existing $5 automatic commission payout to the referrer.
